nodes.question: Is the mug visibly positioned to the right of the headphones?

Absent (no) only if there is clear evidence that no requested change has progressed. Partial if there is evidence of some progress toward moving the mug to the right of the headphones but the requested relationship is not complete. Unknown if required evidence is insufficient or unresolved; do not infer completion, absence, or progress from unrelated edits.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

fulfillment: The binding is too permissive: it asks only whether a mug is to the right of the headphones, so it can mark completion based on any visible mug, without checking that the requested mug was moved from its original position. In the supplied images, the source has one blue mug left of the headphones; the edited image shows a blurred blue remnant on the left and a separate white mug on the right, while the headphones are also altered/cropped. This supports some apparent progress but does not establish that the original mug was moved or that the requested edit is complete. Tighten the node’s typed binding/evidence criteria to track the source mug across the before/after snapshots and assess its displacement relative to the same headphones; distinguish partial progress from a completed relationship, and use unknown if identity or comparison cannot be resolved. The two support observations are highly confident but repeat the same conclusion and do not independently establish object continuity; treat that as an evidence/criterion weakness, not a transport or dependency failure (all checks executed successfully).
s2: The binding checks only the edited image’s final spatial relation, so it can pass for a newly introduced mug and miss whether the requested source mug was moved. Make the typed comparison explicitly use both snapshots: identify the source blue mug and the same headphones, then assess whether that mug’s position changed toward and ultimately to the headphones’ right. Here, the edited image shows a blurred blue remnant on the left and a separate white mug on the right; this is evidence of apparent progress, but does not establish continuity or completion. Preserve partial-progress handling rather than treating the right-side mug alone as fulfillment; use unknown when identity or the comparison cannot be resolved. The headphones also appear altered/cropped, so avoid assuming their identity or position is unchanged. The checks executed successfully: this is a binding/evidence and criterion issue, not a transport or dependency failure. Repeated high-confidence observations of the same final relation are not independent evidence of object continuity.
s1: The node currently tests only whether objects are visible and their final relation is observable; that does not establish whether the requested source mug was moved. Make its typed binding compare the source and edited snapshots, tracking the original blue mug and the same headphones, and record evidence of displacement and final placement. In these images, the source blue mug is left of the headphones; the edit shows a blurred blue remnant on the left and a distinct white mug on the right, with the headphones also changed in appearance/scale. This suggests some progress but does not establish continuity or completion. Preserve partial-progress distinctions, and return unknown when object identity or cross-image comparison is inconclusive rather than treating any right-side mug as fulfillment. The check executed successfully, so address binding/evidence criteria—not transport or dependencies; repeated high-confidence agreement on the final relation is not independent evidence of continuity.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The fulfillment readout is not given the source or edited images, yet its criteria require it to decide whether the original mug remains or whether the right-side mug is additional. The relocation support can report that evidence, but the fulfillment criteria do not faithfully compose its possible outcomes: they allow partial when the original mug remains or the right-side mug is additional, even though the relocation check can fail because the source mug is elsewhere and not to the right, which does not establish progress toward the requested placement. They also do not clearly map a failed relocation check with no progress to absent. Thus the readout can misclassify or leave required cases unresolved.

transaction.reason: The existing supports only establish that some mug is visible to the right of the headphones. Add a nested source-to-edit identity check so the readout can distinguish a completed move from an added mug or ambiguous source remnant, without treating ambiguity as proof of failure.

actions.question: Comparing the source and edited images, does the mug present in the source appear to have been moved to the right of the headphones, rather than a different mug appearing there while the source mug remains elsewhere?
actions.criteria: Pass only when visual continuity or distinctive appearance supports that the source mug is now to the right of the headphones and no separate source mug remains elsewhere. Fail only when clear evidence shows the source mug remains in its original/other location and the right-side mug is a distinct additional mug. Unknown when identity, continuity, or the source location is obscured or ambiguous; a right-side mug alone is insufficient.
actions.binding: Compare source and edited images. Anchor identity to the source image's blue mug left of the headphones; inspect the edited image for that mug's apparent destination and whether a separate mug remains at the source location. Do not infer identity from position alone.

actions.criteria: Apply the original rubric to R1 using all support observations. Complete only if s2 establishes the requested right-side relation and s3 passes, establishing that the source mug was moved there. Partial if there is evidence of progress toward the move (including a right-side mug) but completion is not established, such as s3 failing with clear evidence of an additional mug, or s3 unknown amid suggestive progress. Absent only when evidence establishes no requested progress; do not infer absence from an unknown identity or ambiguous remnant. Unknown when necessary evidence is unresolved and no progress is established. Unrelated edits do not count.

transaction.reason: The existing checks establish only a final-image right-side mug, not whether the source mug moved. Unknown if correspondence or displacement is ambiguous, including when a blurred remnant prevents reliable identification. A right-side mug alone does not establish that the source mug moved.
actions.binding: Inspect both snapshots. Anchor the comparison to the source mug and headphones; assess whether the same mug is identifiable in the edit and whether its position changed relative to the headphones. Report ambiguity rather than inferring identity from position alone.

actions.criteria: Apply the original rubric to R1 using all support observations. Complete only when the requested right-side relationship is established and s3 supports that the source mug was moved there. Partial when evidence shows progress toward the move but completion is not established, including a right-side mug with ambiguous source-mug correspondence or clear evidence of an added mug. Absent only when evidence establishes no requested progress; a failed s3 alone does not establish absence unless it clearly shows no progress. Unknown when necessary evidence is unresolved and progress is not established. Unrelated edits do not count.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The fulfillment readout is not composed faithfully from the saved evidence. It requires s3 to pass for completion, but s3 asks whether the source mug itself moved and explicitly forbids inferring movement from final position alone. The instruction requires only the final spatial relation, not proof of object continuity or a particular editing history. Thus a mug visibly to the right could satisfy the request while s3 remains unknown, yet the program would deny completion. This adds an unsupported mandatory condition. Also, s2’s criteria assign partial when the mug moved toward the target, but its saved observation only checks the final relation and does not establish movement or progress; the readout cannot rely on that unsupported inference.

The program adds an unsupported source-continuity condition to partial-progress judgments. The instruction asks only to move the mug right of the headphones; s3 and the fulfillment criteria require comparison evidence linking the source mug to edited objects before crediting progress. That can leave genuine movement toward the requested position unresolved merely because continuity is unclear, imposing an extra evidentiary constraint not in the rubric. Completion correctly does not require continuity, but the partial/absent composition is therefore not faithful to the original rubric.

The composition rules overlap and can contradict each other. s2 can pass because a mug is to the right, while s3 can establish that this is a distinct added mug and the original remains elsewhere. The fulfillment criteria then say both complete (s2 establishes the requested relation) and partial (s2 shows a right-side mug while s3 establishes it is an addition). The program also adds a source-object continuity condition not present in the instruction: s3’s progress test requires evidence about the original blue mug, although the request only requires a mug to end up right of the headphones. This can wrongly withhold progress when identity is unresolved. Revise the composition to distinguish the requested final-state relation from evidence of progress without making source-object continuity mandatory.

The program adds an unsupported mandatory progress test: s3 requires comparing source and edited images and identifying the source mug by blue color, shape, and an original position left of the headphones, none of which is specified by the instruction or rubric. Although the fulfillment criteria say s3 is not required for completion, they rely on it to establish partial progress when the final relation is not met; this can leave genuine progress unresolved unless that extra identity-based test succeeds. The requested relation itself is adequately checked by s1 and s2, but the program does not faithfully cover the rubric’s progress outcomes without imposing this extra constraint.

The fulfillment readout is not reliably composed from the available evidence. s2 can establish that the final relation fails, but its criteria only call the result partial if the mug moved toward the target; s3 can report source-to-edit evidence, yet its pass/fail criteria are based on whether any mug is to the right and do not require a determinate finding of progress or incompleteness. The readout therefore lacks a clear rule for combining a failed endpoint with s3 evidence to distinguish partial from absent, and may leave known progress unresolved. Also, s3 is activated only after s2 pass, fail, or unknown, so it is always active; this is not itself a defect, but its evidence must be composed explicitly. The requested relation and endpoint are otherwise appropriately specified without imposing editing technique or object continuity.

The fulfillment composition is contradictory and can misclassify progress. It says partial requires evidence of progress, but also says a failed s2 with no evidence of progress is absent only when s3 clearly establishes no progress; otherwise it is unknown. Thus a clearly failed final-state check with unresolved s3 is forced to unknown even though the rubric permits no when no requested change has progressed, and the program does not specify how to resolve that case. Also, s3’s fail criteria combine distinct cases—an additional mug at the target and movement toward but not to the target—while the fulfillment rule assigns partial to the former but absent to the latter if s3 is treated as establishing no progress. This makes the composition depend on an ambiguous support status rather than faithfully distinguishing progress from no progress.

The fulfillment readout is required to use s1, s2, and s3, but s2’s criteria combine the endpoint check with a progress classification that requires source-to-edit evidence unavailable to that check. This overlaps s3’s separate progress check and can produce contradictory progress evidence. Also, s3’s pass/fail status does not encode its separately requested endpoint finding, so the image-free readout cannot reliably compose that finding when s2 is unknown. Separate endpoint and progress evidence cleanly, and ensure the readout can use both without ambiguity.
